sources.title: Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics: Frequently Asked Questions
sources.benefits_coverage: Straight-time wage definitions; excludes listed nonwage compensation categories
sources.methodology: OEWS annual wage convention is 2,080 hours for full-time year-round employment.
limitations: 2,080 is not measured annual productive task time.
Do not multiply a supposed task duration out of salary data.
Occupation medians and whole-economy compensation means are distinct statistics.

sources.title: Employer Costs for Employee Compensation — June 2026
sources.benefits_coverage: Total compensation includes wages/salaries and benefit categories, including paid leave and legally required benefits
sources.methodology: National Compensation Survey employer cost averages; broad private-industry factor is a sensitivity anchor, not occupation-specific total compensation.
limitations: Not a billable service rate.
Applying the ratio to an occupation median combines different populations and dates.
Additional ordinary tooling, management, office and procurement costs remain separate assumptions.

sources.title: Software Developers (15-1252.00)
sources.task_scope: Software modification, testing routines, requirements and project coordination
sources.methodology: Occupational task/activity descriptions; used to map workflow scope to occupation
limitations: Descriptions establish occupational relevance, not task completion times or automation coverage.

sources.title: Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks (43-3031.00)
sources.task_scope: Computing, classifying, recording and checking financial numerical records
limitations: A public synthetic reconciliation workflow is only a bounded analogue of the occupation.

sources.title: Technical Writers (27-3042.00)
sources.task_scope: Technical materials, revision records, editorial standards, changes to prior material
limitations: Does not measure time for source verification, accessible formatting or revisions in this study.

sources.title: Operations Research Analysts (15-2031.00)
sources.task_scope: Modeling and optimization for planning, decision support, time/cost/logistics networks
limitations: Specialist algorithms are ordinary available alternatives; do not assume manual enumeration by a competent human.

sources.title: Wages and Working Time Statistics (COND database)
sources.currency: Local currency and harmonized currency series
sources.benefits_coverage: Earnings exclude employer social-security/pension contributions; labour cost is distinct
sources.methodology: Harmonized series and underlying national statistics; comparison must preserve currency, population and reference period
limitations: No global digital-work total is derived here.
Earnings are not employer total cost; countries cannot be pooled without a currency/time/population rule.

sources.title: EU hourly labour costs ranged from EUR12 to EUR57 in 2025
sources.geography: European Union and euro area; specified activity exclusions
sources.benefits_coverage: Wage and non-wage employer costs; includes some recruitment/training expenditure, less subsidies
sources.methodology: Eurostat labour cost level estimates, dataset lc_lci_lev; source excludes agriculture, public administration/defence, households and extraterritorial activities
limitations: Do not use as US rate, convert silently to dollars, or apply as specialist occupation rate.
Average and median are different statistics.

sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Job Bank / Statistics Canada
sources.title: Technical Writer in the Montreal Region — Wages
sources.benefits_coverage: Published wage rates, not employer total compensation
sources.methodology: Montreal: Statistics Canada Small Area Estimation; Quebec/Canada: Labour Force Survey
limitations: Canonical URL intermittently failed; returned official indexed URL was opened successfully.
No exchange-rate conversion or pooling with US benchmark performed.
Not a task timing study.

sources.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
sources.geography: Study-specific recruited open-source developers; not a nationally representative sample
sources.occupation: Experienced developers in familiar mature projects
sources.methodology: Randomized permission to use AI per task; completion time comparison
sources.ai_usage: Explicitly randomized allowed vs disallowed; allowed arm predominantly Cursor Pro and Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet
limitations: Historical tooling and specific familiar-codebase setting.
Effect must not be imported as a multiplier for this study.
Preserves a losing comparison and motivates full workflow timing.

sources.title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
sources.geography: Study-specific college-educated professionals; not occupation-population representative
sources.methodology: Preregistered randomized exposure to ChatGPT; final journal abstract reports 453 participants
sources.ai_usage: Explicit intervention; primary abstract states half exposed to ChatGPT
limitations: Journal full-text open was blocked; primary publisher search abstract and Stanford academic abstract agree.
Accessible earlier MIT manuscript has n=444 and standardized-effect reporting; do not conflate manuscript versions.
Does not establish present-agent autonomous quality, these study task times or a general market effect.

sources.publisher: arXiv; subsequent Quarterly Journal of Economics publication
sources.title: Generative AI at Work
sources.reference_period: Firm-specific deployment period reported in paper
sources.task_scope: Issues resolved per hour among 5,172 support agents
sources.methodology: Staggered introduction of an assistive conversational system; heterogeneous worker effects
sources.ai_usage: Explicit tool introduction; human workers remain in workflow
limitations: Version 1 had different sample/effect figures; v2 is pinned.
Support involving private customer data is outside this study’s permitted inputs.
Evidence motivates capability transfer and heterogeneity; numerical effect is not a simulation calibration for unrelated workflows.

comparison_rules.primary: Competent human production using ordinary non-AI tools, matched acceptance criteria; no observed human panel in this study
comparison_rules.human_expected_cost: W_h * E[total human hours including revisions and unsuccessful work allocated per accepted output] + ordinary_tool_and_business_cost_per_accepted_output
comparison_rules.task_time_grid_classification: assumed sensitivity grid, not measured or sourced duration
comparison_rules.benefit_factor_grid_classification: assumed scenarios; central factor is derived from ECEC totals, not occupation-specific observation
comparison_rules.quality_rule: Only compare deliverables satisfying the same acceptance standard. Excluded unsupported quality is not inferred from a fast kernel.
comparison_rules.incumbent_rule: Competent humans may use strong conventional specialist software; do not use manual enumeration or needless retyping as a straw-man baseline.
